notes: Diff is a single new test file (server/internal/httpapi/external_api_test.go, +237). No production code, no config, no migration, no dependency change - revert is a plain file deletion, risk of regression on merge is confined to CI time.

Mutation-checked the assertions against internal/httpapi/external_api.go (patched, ran, restored; worktree verified clean afterwards). All five mutations were caught: dropping the Retry-After header (test:52), keying the limiter on a constant instead of credential.KeyID (test:60), dropping the 'api-key:' prefix on the audit actor name (test:162), dropping the WWW-Authenticate header (test:98), and handing the principal a fixed scope set instead of credential.Scopes (test:140). These are not no-op characterization tests.

The three 401 sub-cases are genuinely distinct paths, not duplicates: apikeys.Service.Authenticate (service.go:559) short-circuits on `!HasPrefix("ivq_sk_") || len<40`, so "not-an-invenqor-key" fails the prefix guard while the 48-char "ivq_sk_..." case reaches the DB lookup and returns ErrUnauthorized from sql.ErrNoRows.

The comment claim that nothing exercised /api/v1/external/* over an API key checks out - grep for 'api/v1/external' across *_test.go finds no other hit; the existing MCP tests use a key against /mcp, which shares the middleware but not the routes under test.

go vet ./internal/httpapi passes and the full package suite passes (12.1s). The new tests build their own Server per test, so mutating server.apiRateLimit (test:32) cannot leak into the MCP tests that share the same middleware and default 600/min limiter.

Nit, no action needed: external_api.go:25 hardcodes `Retry-After: 60` rather than deriving it from the limiter window, and the test asserts "60" with the comment "want the window in seconds" while itself configuring a 1-minute window. The assertion is correct today but would not catch a future window change desynchronising from the header.

Nit: the audit assertion at test:157 uses QueryRow with no ORDER BY/LIMIT on `SELECT actor_name FROM audit_logs WHERE action='asset.create'`. Only one such row exists in this test, so it is deterministic now; it would become order-dependent if the test ever created a second asset.
